name: PartlyGood Topic Taxonomy
description: Evolution of the PartlyGood taxonomy. v1.1 adds an explicit cross-cutting topic dimension, topic governance metadata, and a changelog, while preserving every v1.0 topic id for backward compatibility with published pieces.

cross_cutting.rationale: Several AI capabilities serve every field. v1.0 already carried them under the ai.* prefix; v1.1 names them explicitly as a cross-cutting dimension so a piece can be tagged cross-cutting without being misread as a single field's asset.

governance.versioning: SemVer-style MAJOR.MINOR. Each taxonomy change ships as a new taxonomy-v<MAJOR.MINOR>.json file; the previous file stays on disk so validators can diff for backward compatibility. MINOR: additive only (new topics, new metadata, new cross-cutting flags). MAJOR: any removal, rename, or repurposing of an existing topic id.
governance.backward_compatibility: Existing topic ids are never removed or renamed in a MINOR release. A new topic may be added only if no published piece already uses the id for a different meaning. When a topic id must change, that is a MAJOR change requiring an editorial migration and a content audit before release.
governance.who_can_add_topics: Any publisher / engineer may propose a new topic by opening an issue that names the topic id, the field it belongs to, a one-line scope, and (for cross-cutting) the fields it applies to. The Taxonomy owner (Founding Engineer) approves; the CEO owns editorial intent and may veto. No topic is added by a single contributor merging code without a review comment on the issue.
governance.who_can_merge_topics: Topic merges are MAJOR changes and require: (1) a decision on the issue with a named Taxonomy owner, (2) the merged topic's id chosen to keep the most-published id or redirect content, and (3) a published notice before the merge lands so existing pieces can be re-tagged.
governance.update_process: 1) Open a taxonomy issue describing the change. 2) Branch or worktree off main. 3) Ship the new taxonomy-v<MAJOR.MINOR>.json. 4) Run scripts/taxonomy_compat.py to prove no existing topic id was dropped. 5) Update research/scripts/taxonomy.py if its load path changed. 6) Update docs/taxonomy.md and any references. 7) Run validate_content.py + quality_checks.py. 8) Merge on green. 9) Record the change in the changelog.
governance.conflict_resolution: Escalate conflicting field/scope edits to the CEO (editorial intent).
